description.describe_ch: This course aims at helping students who are planning to pursue undergraduate studies oversea. It develops students applied academic writing skills. The teaching unit include a full process of compiling an individual research project—poetic autoethnography—which students need to work on identifying research questions, locating academic sources, correcting data, discussing data to answer their research questions, and making oral presentations

gradeRuleDescribe.tpa_score_new:
Course Participation 50%
  • Attendance 10% (This grade reflects your physical attendance, active engagement in class activities, and the completion of pre-class online tasks.)
    • Pre-Class Self-Learning Modules: To accommodate the 16-week academic calendar, six asynchronous online modules (instructional videos + quizzes) will be assigned on the learning platform throughout the semester. You must complete these modules before our designated in-class writing sessions.
    • Grading & Penalty: These quizzes are graded based on completion, not accuracy. However, they are strictly mandatory. At the end of the semester, one point will be explicitly deducted from your final participation grade for every uncompleted module.
  • Online Weekly Entries (Tasks & Final Class Reflection) 40%
    • The scores of online entries depend on the completeness of your class reflections or tasks assigned.
Final Project 50%
  • Poetic Autoethnography 30%
  • Presentation 20%

gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol:
A.  Attendance: This class is designed so that knowledge is developed throughout the semester and involves a series of in-class lectures, discussions, workshops, and activities. Accordingly, missing class is a serious issue and will result in you being unable to complete the class assignments.  If you miss more than 10-hour of class (including all leaves), you will automatically receive an “F” score for this course. If you must miss class, please apply for the leaves on the FCU system and notify me in advance. All leaves require valid documents, including parental signature for general leaves, doctoral and clinic receipts for sick leaves, wedding invitations, correctly dated photos, etc. You are expected to come to the next class fully prepared. PowerPoint slides and materials used in class will be on iLearn. 

B.	Plagiarism: Plagiarism is defined as “using someone else’s words, original ideas, or data in your work of writing without giving proper credit or reference to the creator. In other words, you present another person’s ideas as your own” (IUP Writing Center, para 1). This is a very serious issue that can result in the possibility of expulsion from the university. The penalty for plagiarism can be a failure for this course. Violations of academic integrity will not be tolerated. A lesson on how to avoid plagiarism and cite sources appropriately will be given in class.

C.	Late Work: No late work will be accepted. Not being in class does not excuse you from presenting your work on time, excluding class reflection entries. If you have a legitimate reason for being late with work, you must communicate by email with me before the deadline. Decisions regarding this matter will be made at the instructor’s discretion. Even in this case, your grade will not be as good as it would be when you submit your work on time. You should make sure that you always save your work and have backup files. Lost files or laptop or printer breakdown cannot be an excuse for your late work.

D.	Email/iLearn: You must check your FCU email OR iLearn daily. FCU email/iLearn is the main communication method with the instructor and the best way for you to reach me to ask questions or discuss your concerns. I will respond to student emails/iLearn messages during the semester within 48 hours. If you don’t get a response within 48 hours, please send me a reminder. If you decide to contact me via email, please use your FCU email addresses. If I need to cancel class, I will contact you via iLearn.

E.	Electronic Devices:  Cell phones should be switched off or on mute during class. Laptops or tablets are permitted when having in-class writing assignments. However, if you expect an emergency or important call, you may inform me and leave the cell phone on.

F.     AI Policy Statement: In this course, I encourage you to use Generative AI responsibly as a collaborative tool, provided you adhere to the principles of "transparency" and "critical engagement." However, you must adhere to the following policies in the class: 

1.	Duty of Transparency: You are not required to hide your use of AI, but you must be explicit about how you have used it in some of your weekly entries as critical reflections. You must document: the prompts you used, the suggestions you accepted or rejected, and your reasoning behind these decisions—specifically how they helped or hindered your development of an analytical voice.
2.	Authorial Responsibility: Regardless of AI assistance, you retain full academic responsibility for your final submission. AI can produce fluent prose that masks limited engagement with ideas; please remember that I am assessing your analytical depth, critical reasoning, and ability to engage with scholarly arguments, not merely the production of text.

gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol_en:
A.  Attendance: This class is designed so that knowledge is developed throughout the semester and involves a series of in-class lectures, discussions, workshops, and activities. Accordingly, missing class is a serious issue and will result in you being unable to complete the class assignments.  If you miss more than 10-hour of class (including all leaves), you will automatically receive an “F” score for this course. If you must miss class, please apply for the leaves on the FCU system and notify me in advance. All leaves require valid documents, including parental signature for general leaves, doctoral and clinic receipts for sick leaves, wedding invitations, correctly dated photos, etc. You are expected to come to the next class fully prepared. PowerPoint slides and materials used in class will be on iLearn. 

B.	Plagiarism: Plagiarism is defined as “using someone else’s words, original ideas, or data in your work of writing without giving proper credit or reference to the creator. In other words, you present another person’s ideas as your own” (IUP Writing Center, para 1). This is a very serious issue that can result in the possibility of expulsion from the university. The penalty for plagiarism can be a failure for this course. Violations of academic integrity will not be tolerated. A lesson on how to avoid plagiarism and cite sources appropriately will be given in class.

C.	Late Work: No late work will be accepted. Not being in class does not excuse you from presenting your work on time, excluding class reflection entries. If you have a legitimate reason for being late with work, you must communicate by email with me before the deadline. Decisions regarding this matter will be made at the instructor’s discretion. Even in this case, your grade will not be as good as it would be when you submit your work on time. You should make sure that you always save your work and have backup files. Lost files or laptop or printer breakdown cannot be an excuse for your late work.

D.	Email/iLearn: You must check your FCU email OR iLearn daily. FCU email/iLearn is the main communication method with the instructor and the best way for you to reach me to ask questions or discuss your concerns. I will respond to student emails/iLearn messages during the semester within 48 hours. If you don’t get a response within 48 hours, please send me a reminder. If you decide to contact me via email, please use your FCU email addresses. If I need to cancel class, I will contact you via iLearn.

E.	Electronic Devices:  Cell phones should be switched off or on mute during class. Laptops or tablets are permitted when having in-class writing assignments. However, if you expect an emergency or important call, you may inform me and leave the cell phone on.

F.     AI Policy Statement: In this course, I encourage you to use Generative AI responsibly as a collaborative tool, provided you adhere to the principles of "transparency" and "critical engagement." However, you must adhere to the policies addressed under "Academic Integrity" of the syllabus.
gradeRuleDescribe.ais_meno:
Plagiarism 瞟竊規範
  • 考核時如果您抄襲他人的答案、或交作業時您交出全部或部分由他人撰寫的論文或作業，則被視為作弊。剽竊是對學術信任的嚴重破壞。在學習作業中，我們的言論和想法就是我們作業的價值；因此將他人的作品當作自己的作品繳交，是一種盜竊行為。當您使用別人的文字和想法時，無論是著名作家還是同學的作品，而不註明這些文章、詞語和想法的來源出處，您的行為就是在抄襲。原創性作品是我的底線，抄襲的作品將會收到“0”或“不及格”的分數。
  • Plagiarism: Plagiarism is defined as “using someone else’s words, original ideas, or data in your work of writing without giving proper credit or reference to the creator. In other words, you present another person’s ideas as your own” (IUP Writing Center, para 1). This is a very serious issue that can result in the possibility of expulsion from the university. The penalty for plagiarism can be a failure for this course. Violations of academic integrity will not be tolerated. A lesson on how to avoid plagiarism and cite sources appropriately will be given in class.
AI 使用規範 (AI Policy Statement)
  • 在本課程中，我鼓勵各位負責任地使用生成式 AI 作為協作工具，但必須遵守『公開透明』與『批判性檢視』原則。
    • 透明化義務： 您不必隱瞞 AI 的使用，但您必須在某些週的作業中明確說明您如何使用它。您需要記錄：您輸入了什麼提示詞 (Prompts)、您採納了哪些建議、您拒絕了哪些建議，以及為什麼您認為這些建議能（或不能）提升您的寫作邏輯與聲音。
    • 作者責任： 無論 AI 提供多少輔助，您必須對最終提交的文件負起所有學術責任。AI 可能會生成流暢但內容空洞的文字；請記住，評分的標準在於您個人的分析深度、批判思考以及與文獻進行對話的能力，而非僅是文本的產出。
    • 禁止事項： 禁止未經審核直接複製貼上 AI 的輸出內容。若您的作業中出現未註明的 AI 生成內容，將視同抄襲。請記住，我們致力於培養的是『具備獨立思考的寫作者』，而非文字自動化生成器。」
  • In this course, I encourage you to use Generative AI responsibly as a collaborative tool, provided you adhere to the principles of "transparency" and "critical engagement." However, you must adhere to the following policies in the class:
    • Duty of Transparency: You are not required to hide your use of AI, but you must be explicit about how you have used it in some of your weekly entries as critical reflections. You must document: the prompts you used, the suggestions you accepted or rejected, and your reasoning behind these decisions—specifically how they helped or hindered your development of an analytical voice.
    • Authorial Responsibility: Regardless of AI assistance, you retain full academic responsibility for your final submission. AI can produce fluent prose that masks limited engagement with ideas; please remember that I am assessing your analytical depth, critical reasoning, and ability to engage with scholarly arguments, not merely the production of text.
    • Prohibited Actions: Copying and pasting AI-generated content without attribution is strictly prohibited and will be treated as plagiarism. Remember, my goal is to cultivate 'writers who can think and inquire,' not text-assembly generators."

    • Grading & Penalty: These quizzes are graded based on completion, not accuracy. However, they are strictly mandatory. At the end of the semester, one point will be explicitly deducted from your final participation grade for every uncompleted module.
  • Online Weekly Entries (Tasks & Final Class Reflection) 40%
    • The scores of online entries depend on the completeness of your class reflections or tasks assigned.
Final Project 50%
  • Poetic Autoethnography 30%
  • Presentation 20%
policy.course_pol:
A.  Attendance: This class is designed so that knowledge is developed throughout the semester and involves a series of in-class lectures, discussions, workshops, and activities. Accordingly, missing class is a serious issue and will result in you being unable to complete the class assignments.  If you miss more than 10-hour of class (including all leaves), you will automatically receive an “F” score for this course. If you must miss class, please apply for the leaves on the FCU system and notify me in advance. All leaves require valid documents, including parental signature for general leaves, doctoral and clinic receipts for sick leaves, wedding invitations, correctly dated photos, etc. You are expected to come to the next class fully prepared. PowerPoint slides and materials used in class will be on iLearn. 

B.	Plagiarism: Plagiarism is defined as “using someone else’s words, original ideas, or data in your work of writing without giving proper credit or reference to the creator. In other words, you present another person’s ideas as your own” (IUP Writing Center, para 1). This is a very serious issue that can result in the possibility of expulsion from the university. The penalty for plagiarism can be a failure for this course. Violations of academic integrity will not be tolerated. A lesson on how to avoid plagiarism and cite sources appropriately will be given in class.

C.	Late Work: No late work will be accepted. Not being in class does not excuse you from presenting your work on time, excluding class reflection entries. If you have a legitimate reason for being late with work, you must communicate by email with me before the deadline. Decisions regarding this matter will be made at the instructor’s discretion. Even in this case, your grade will not be as good as it would be when you submit your work on time. You should make sure that you always save your work and have backup files. Lost files or laptop or printer breakdown cannot be an excuse for your late work.

D.	Email/iLearn: You must check your FCU email OR iLearn daily. FCU email/iLearn is the main communication method with the instructor and the best way for you to reach me to ask questions or discuss your concerns. I will respond to student emails/iLearn messages during the semester within 48 hours. If you don’t get a response within 48 hours, please send me a reminder. If you decide to contact me via email, please use your FCU email addresses. If I need to cancel class, I will contact you via iLearn.

E.	Electronic Devices:  Cell phones should be switched off or on mute during class. Laptops or tablets are permitted when having in-class writing assignments. However, if you expect an emergency or important call, you may inform me and leave the cell phone on.

F.     AI Policy Statement: In this course, I encourage you to use Generative AI responsibly as a collaborative tool, provided you adhere to the principles of "transparency" and "critical engagement." However, you must adhere to the following policies in the class: 

1.	Duty of Transparency: You are not required to hide your use of AI, but you must be explicit about how you have used it in some of your weekly entries as critical reflections. You must document: the prompts you used, the suggestions you accepted or rejected, and your reasoning behind these decisions—specifically how they helped or hindered your development of an analytical voice.
2.	Authorial Responsibility: Regardless of AI assistance, you retain full academic responsibility for your final submission. AI can produce fluent prose that masks limited engagement with ideas; please remember that I am assessing your analytical depth, critical reasoning, and ability to engage with scholarly arguments, not merely the production of text.
3.	Prohibited Actions: Copying and pasting AI-generated content without attribution is strictly prohibited and will be treated as plagiarism. Remember, my goal is to cultivate 'writers who can think and inquire,' not text-assembly generators."

policy.ais_meno:
Plagiarism 瞟竊規範
  • 考核時如果您抄襲他人的答案、或交作業時您交出全部或部分由他人撰寫的論文或作業，則被視為作弊。剽竊是對學術信任的嚴重破壞。在學習作業中，我們的言論和想法就是我們作業的價值；因此將他人的作品當作自己的作品繳交，是一種盜竊行為。當您使用別人的文字和想法時，無論是著名作家還是同學的作品，而不註明這些文章、詞語和想法的來源出處，您的行為就是在抄襲。原創性作品是我的底線，抄襲的作品將會收到“0”或“不及格”的分數。
  • Plagiarism: Plagiarism is defined as “using someone else’s words, original ideas, or data in your work of writing without giving proper credit or reference to the creator. In other words, you present another person’s ideas as your own” (IUP Writing Center, para 1). This is a very serious issue that can result in the possibility of expulsion from the university. The penalty for plagiarism can be a failure for this course. Violations of academic integrity will not be tolerated. A lesson on how to avoid plagiarism and cite sources appropriately will be given in class.
AI 使用規範 (AI Policy Statement)
  • 在本課程中，我鼓勵各位負責任地使用生成式 AI 作為協作工具，但必須遵守『公開透明』與『批判性檢視』原則。
    • 透明化義務： 您不必隱瞞 AI 的使用，但您必須在某些週的作業中明確說明您如何使用它。您需要記錄：您輸入了什麼提示詞 (Prompts)、您採納了哪些建議、您拒絕了哪些建議，以及為什麼您認為這些建議能（或不能）提升您的寫作邏輯與聲音。
    • 作者責任： 無論 AI 提供多少輔助，您必須對最終提交的文件負起所有學術責任。AI 可能會生成流暢但內容空洞的文字；請記住，評分的標準在於您個人的分析深度、批判思考以及與文獻進行對話的能力，而非僅是文本的產出。
    • 禁止事項： 禁止未經審核直接複製貼上 AI 的輸出內容。若您的作業中出現未註明的 AI 生成內容，將視同抄襲。請記住，我們致力於培養的是『具備獨立思考的寫作者』，而非文字自動化生成器。」
  • In this course, I encourage you to use Generative AI responsibly as a collaborative tool, provided you adhere to the principles of "transparency" and "critical engagement." However, you must adhere to the following policies in the class:
    • Duty of Transparency: You are not required to hide your use of AI, but you must be explicit about how you have used it in some of your weekly entries as critical reflections. You must document: the prompts you used, the suggestions you accepted or rejected, and your reasoning behind these decisions—specifically how they helped or hindered your development of an analytical voice.
    • Authorial Responsibility: Regardless of AI assistance, you retain full academic responsibility for your final submission. AI can produce fluent prose that masks limited engagement with ideas; please remember that I am assessing your analytical depth, critical reasoning, and ability to engage with scholarly arguments, not merely the production of text.
    • Prohibited Actions: Copying and pasting AI-generated content without attribution is strictly prohibited and will be treated as plagiarism. Remember, my goal is to cultivate 'writers who can think and inquire,' not text-assembly generators."
